key_insight: Large language models can be repurposed to interpret wearable IMU streams and reconstruct 4D human motion plus surrounding 3D scene layouts—enabling perception without cameras.
problem_solved: Addresses reliance on cameras for human-scene understanding by providing a privacy-preserving, low-power, and scalable alternative that reconstructs motion and scene geometry purely from everyday wearable sensors (IMUs).
method: Collect continuous IMU streams from body-worn sensors and encode them into compact spatiotemporal token sequences.
Repurpose and fine-tune an LLM-style spatiotemporal reasoning backbone to map IMU tokens to 3D human poses and scene layout over time (4D).
Train and validate on mixed real and synthetic data with geometry-aware losses to reconstruct temporally consistent motion and 3D scene elements without visual inputs.
impact: Enables privacy-preserving, energy-efficient sensing pipelines for AR, assistive tech, and robotics; introduces a template for applying LLM-style reasoning to non-visual time-series perception tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: wearable IMUs → token encoder → LLM reasoning → 4D output (animated skeleton + scene geometry).
Before/after visualization: raw IMU traces vs. reconstructed 3D motion and scene overlays.
Bar chart: trade-offs comparing camera vs. IMU-based systems on privacy, energy, and deployment scalability.
Qualitative timeline: short animated frames showing temporally consistent 4D reconstruction (motion + scene) from IMU-only input.
paper_title: Seeing Without Eyes: 4D Human-Scene Understanding from Wearable IMUs
paper_authors: Hao-Yu Hsu, Tianhang Cheng, Jing Wen, Alexander G. Schwing, Shenlong Wang
